rounds.text: Jindal Drilling & Industries Ltd is currently priced at a significant discount to its intrinsic value, trading at a P/B ratio of 0.98x compared to the sector benchmark of 2.26x [E7]. This valuation disconnect is further highlighted by the company’s superior operational efficiency, as evidenced by an ROE of 11.57% which nearly doubles the sector benchmark of 6.41% [E9]. The company’s ability to generate value is underscored by an ROA of 8.24%, a stark contrast to the sector benchmark of -72.76% [E8]. While the stock trades at a P/E of 9.82x [E1], this remains highly attractive when measured against the broader sector benchmark of -78.79x [E6]. Conceded: the dividend yield is a negligible 0.17% [E4], and the 10-year median ROE of 7% suggests historical performance has been lower than current levels [E26]. Nevertheless, the consistent upward trend in median ROE from 7% over 10 years to 13% over the last year demonstrates a clear improvement in capital efficiency [E26, E29].

Jindal Drilling & Industries Ltd presents a long-term performance profile that raises significant questions regarding its ability to generate consistent shareholder value. While recent metrics show improvement, the company’s 10-year median return on equity stands at a lackluster 7% [E26]. This historical underperformance is underscored by the fact that the company is explicitly flagged for having a low return on equity of 11.4% over the last three years [E63]. Furthermore, investors seeking income are poorly served by the current dividend yield of 0.17% [E4]. Conceded: the company currently trades at a P/E of 9.82x [E1] and maintains a P/B ratio of 0.98x, which is notably lower than the sector benchmark of 2.26x [E7]. Despite these valuation multiples, the persistent gap between long-term historical returns and recent performance suggests that the current market capitalisation of ₹ 1,722 Cr may be pricing in a level of operational efficiency that the company has struggled to sustain over the past decade [E3, E26].
